title: SCAR: Scheduling Multi-Model AI Workloads on Heterogeneous Multi-Chiplet Module Accelerators
problem: Scheduling multi-model workloads on heterogeneous dataflow MCM AI accelerators is computationally intractable, reaching O(10^56) even for two-model workloads on 6×6 chiplets. Previous homogeneous MCM accelerators with fixed dataflows lack the workload adaptivity needed for diverse multi-model scenarios.
motivation: Emerging multi-model workloads with heavy models like LLMs require scalable and adaptive hardware architectures to meet increasing compute and memory demands.
method: SCAR develops heuristics to navigate the massive scheduling space for heterogeneous dataflow MCM accelerators. The scheduler incorporates advanced techniques such as inter-chiplet pipelining to optimize workload placement and execution across chiplets. The approach is evaluated on ten multi-model workload scenarios for datacenter multitenancy and AR/VR use-cases.
key_novelty: First scheduler to exploit heterogeneous dataflow support in MCM accelerators with inter-chiplet pipelining to adaptively handle diverse multi-model workloads.
contributions: Identifies and formalizes the multi-model scheduling problem on heterogeneous dataflow MCM accelerators
Develops SCAR scheduler with practical heuristics including inter-chiplet pipelining
Demonstrates 27.6-29.6% EDP improvements over homogeneous baselines across datacenter and AR/VR workloads
Comprehensive evaluation framework for multi-model scheduling on heterogeneous accelerators
primary_theme: Multi-model scheduling on heterogeneous multi-chiplet accelerators
